United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 123A9426C0010
In accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) FAR
12.102 (a), the following documents the decision to restrict competition for this acquisition.
(1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity.
Requisition Number: 1168172 and 1168366
Requesting Activity Agency: FSIS-OPHS
Contracting Activity: FSIS-OM-PcMB
(2) Estimated Value
Period	Fiscal Year	Total
BASE	FY26	$65,000.00
Option 1	FY27	$65,000.00
Option 2	FY28	$65,000.00
Option 3	FY29	$65,000.00
Option 4	FY30	$65,000.00
Subtotal	$325,000.00
Evaluation of FAR 52.217-8	$32,500.00
Grand Total	$357,500.00
(3) Brief Description of Supplies or Services
US Department of Agriculture (USDA), Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) requires
maintenance, calibration, technical support, and software update services for the proprietary ViewPoint
Continuous Environmental Monitoring System manufactured by Mesa Laboratories. This includes
support for ViewPoint VPx, VPx Pro 6, and Essentials hardware components such as sensors, probes,
and communication devices; the ViewPoint software applications (on‑premises and cloud); and the
CheckPoint hardware line. The services must follow Mesa Laboratories’ proprietary installation,
calibration, and validation procedures, which ensure system integrity and compliance with their
ISO/IEC 17025:2017 accredited Quality Assurance processes.
(4) Suggested Source
The suggested contractor is:
MESA LABORATORIES INC.
12100 W 6TH AVE.
LAKEWOOD, CO 80228-1252
UEI: N36KBDHE4D23
(5) Justification for Restricting Competition and the Basis for that Decision.
Page 1 of 3
Rev. 3/4/26

United States Department of Agriculture
Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold
Identification Number: 123A9426C0010
A. Explain the unique qualifications/characteristics of the proposed contractor or product and why no
other contractor or product/service can meet the Government's need.
Mesa Laboratories, Inc. is the sole manufacturer, intellectual property rights holder, and exclusive
authorized provider of all ViewPoint hardware, software, and related continuous environmental
monitoring components. All ViewPoint sensors and probes are manufactured using Mesa
Laboratories trade secrets and undergo proprietary calibration and quality assurance processes. The
ViewPoint software is developed solely for use with Mesa Laboratories hardware and may only be
updated, upgraded, patched, or serviced by Mesa Laboratories personnel under authorized
customer support agreements. The combination of proprietary hardware, software licensing
restrictions, and integrated system architecture prevents third‑party vendors from servicing,
repairing, or modifying any part of the system. Mesa Laboratories does not authorize any
third‑party contractor to install, calibrate, or service its Continuous Monitoring Systems; any such
action voids warranties and may invalidate service agreements. Because FSIS relies on installed
proprietary systems that must be serviced exclusively by the manufacturer to remain functional and
compliant, competition is not feasible.
B. Describe market research conducted and the results or the reason why no market research was
conducted.
Market research determined that Mesa Laboratories does not authorize third‑party service providers to
sell, install, calibrate, or maintain the ViewPoint Continuous Environmental Monitoring System. The
proprietary nature of both the hardware and software, combined with licensing restrictions, prevents
any alternative sources from providing compliant maintenance or support. Installation, calibration, and
validation require Mesa‑trained technicians using proprietary Installation and Operational
Qualification (IOQ) protocols, and any attempt by non‑authorized personnel may void warranties and
result in the cancellation of support agreements. Based on this research and manufacturer
documentation, Mesa Laboratories is the only source capable of meeting FSIS operational
requirements.
FSIS continues to review emerging environmental monitoring technologies to determine whether
competitive, non‑proprietary alternatives may meet future laboratory requirements. However, replacing
the current installed ViewPoint system would require a complete overhaul of hardware, software,
sensor arrays, and facility validation procedures—resulting in significant operational disruption and
considerably higher cost. For this current requirement, no commercially available alternatives can
interface with or service the existing proprietary Mesa Laboratories system. FSIS will continue to
conduct market research in future acquisition planning cycles to identify competitive opportunities
when they become viable.
Certifications & Approvals

I certify this requirement meets the Government’s minimum need and that the supporting data, which
forms a basis for this justification, is complete and accurate.

results.summary:
This **Decision to Restrict Competition under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold**, issued by the **U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)**, documents the agency’s determination to procure maintenance, calibration, technical support, and software-update services for its proprietary **Mesa Laboratories ViewPoint Continuous Environmental Monitoring System** exclusively from Mesa Laboratories, Inc.

The requirement supports FSIS-OPHS under requisitions 1168172 and 1168366 and covers ViewPoint VPx, VPx Pro 6, Essentials hardware—including sensors, probes, and communications equipment—the on-premises and cloud-based ViewPoint applications, and the CheckPoint hardware line.

Services must use Mesa’s proprietary installation, calibration, validation, and quality-assurance procedures consistent with its ISO/IEC 17025:2017-accredited processes.

The acquisition is planned for a five-year period, with a $65,000 base period in FY2026 and four $65,000 option periods in FY2027–FY2030, totaling $325,000 before a stated grand total of $357,500.

The recommended source is **Mesa Laboratories, Inc., 12100 W. 6th Avenue, Lakewood, Colorado 80228-1252**, UEI N36KBDHE4D23.

FSIS determined that Mesa is the sole manufacturer, intellectual-property holder, and exclusive authorized provider for the ViewPoint system. Its proprietary hardware, software licensing, trade-secret manufacturing methods, and integrated architecture prevent third parties from performing authorized repairs, updates, calibration, installation, or validation.

Market research confirmed that Mesa does not authorize other providers to sell, install, calibrate, or maintain the system and that only Mesa-trained technicians can perform the required Installation and Operational Qualification procedures.

FSIS concluded that using non-authorized personnel could void warranties, terminate support agreements, compromise system functionality, and affect compliance.

Although FSIS is monitoring future nonproprietary alternatives, replacing the installed system would require extensive hardware, software, sensor-array, and facility-validation changes, causing significant disruption and higher costs. Therefore, competition is not feasible for the current requirement.
